data.title: Command and Scripting Interpreter Abuse
data.summary: The sample's logic runs substantially as script — PowerShell, a Windows Script Host language, a shell script — rather than as compiled native code, often invoked by a small native or document-embedded loader.
data.description:
Running as script changes the detection surface entirely: there is no PE file to scan once
the interpreter itself (a legitimate, signed system binary) is doing the executing, and
the actual logic lives in command-line arguments, a script file, or content piped via
stdin that standard file-based AV scanning may never see as a discrete artefact. Script-
block logging and command-line auditing, where enabled, are usually the only reliable
record of what actually ran.
data.recommendation:
* Enable and review script-block and command-line logging for the interpreter in use; file-based scanning alone will not have seen this payload.
* Recover the full script content, not only the invoking command line — payloads are frequently passed encoded or staged from a second location the command line only references.
* Restrict interpreter execution policy and constrained-language modes where the environment allows, to reduce what an arbitrary script is permitted to do even if it runs.
data.short_recommendation: Enable script-block and command-line logging for the interpreter; file-based scanning will not have seen this payload.

mitre_techniques.procedure: A macro launched PowerShell with an encoded command argument that decoded and executed a staged script in memory.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Core payload logic executed as an in-memory PowerShell script rather than a compiled native binary.
